content.title: About
content.content: A turkey hot dog is a sausage made from turkey meat served in a soft bun. Turkey provides a milder flavor and lower fat content compared with traditional beef hot dogs, making it a lighter snack option.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey contains roughly half the calories of beef for the same serving size while delivering similar protein.
The hot dog tradition started in the United States in the late 19th century; turkey versions have become popular in health‑focused diets.
Turkey is rich in tryptophan, an amino acid that supports serotonin production.
Some markets offer whole‑grain buns to boost the nutritional profile of the snack.
Turkey hot dogs are often served with mustard, ketchup, or low‑sugar barbecue sauce.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Turkey meat contains less saturated fat, helping to maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A single turkey hot dog provides about 15‑20 g of protein, essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey supplies niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Moderate calorie count
items.content: One turkey hot dog typically contains 250‑300 kcal, suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium supports immune function and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey meat.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processed turkey sausages often contain added salt, so people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain products may contain nitrites or other preservatives, which should be limited.

items.title: Gluten in the bun
items.content: Standard buns contain gluten, making the snack unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the hot dog in the microwave or on a grill, split the bun, add mustard, ketchup, fresh veggies or slaw. It pairs well with fries or a cabbage salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated hot dogs at 0‑4 °C for up to 3 days. Frozen versions can be stored for up to 2 months in an airtight package.
